threatModelSummary: This is local-only Playwright test fixture infrastructure for E2E-testing CesiumJS globes — a dev dependency, never shipped to production, with no auth, no user accounts, no persisted data, and no network exposure beyond a server bound explicitly to 127.0.0.1. The only component that parses input shaped like it crosses a trust boundary is fixtures/serve.mjs, a static file server invoked by Playwright's webServer during test runs; it serves Cesium's bundled assets and the fixture's own planet texture. STRIDE was applied with that server, the pure geometry module (src/geometry.ts), and the Cesium page-evaluate seam (src/fixture.ts) as the surfaces of interest. The one finding worth recording was a dependency-version drift (vitest pinned to an old major pulling in a vite release with a known high-severity advisory) rather than a code-level flaw; it has been fixed directly. The static file server's path-resolution guard was verified by hand with both raw and URL-encoded `../` traversal attempts and correctly returns 404 for both while still serving legitimate assets.
dependencyAudit: pnpm audit --audit-level=high (full workspace) flagged packages__saturday-playwright-cesium>vitest>vite as High: 'launch-editor fs.existsSync() bypass on Windows' (GHSA-587h-7wmj-h5pm), caused by this package pinning vitest ^2.1.9 while every other package in the monorepo (saturday-core, saturday-cucumber, saturday-cucumber-indexer, saturday-ml-analyzer, saturday-playwright, saturday-playwright-heatmap) pins ^4.0.16.

Fixed: bumped packages/saturday-playwright-cesium/package.json's vitest devDependency from ^2.1.9 to ^4.0.16 to match the rest of the monorepo, ran pnpm install, and confirmed via pnpm audit that this package no longer appears in any High or Critical finding. Re-ran `pnpm vitest run` under the new version — all 7 geometry.spec.ts tests pass unchanged.
No other new dependency (cesium@1.146.0, @playwright/test) produced a High or Critical finding in the scoped audit output.

stride.assessed: No authentication, sessions, or identity of any kind exists in this package — it is a local test-fixture server and a Playwright page-evaluate seam. Not applicable.

The only externally-reachable input is the HTTP request path to fixtures/serve.mjs. resolveWithinRoot() resolves the path against each route's root directory and rejects any result that does not start with that root (with a trailing separator, closing the classic prefix-bypass gap). Verified by hand: both `GET /assets/../../../../etc/passwd` and its %2e%2e-encoded form return 404; legitimate assets under /assets/ and /cesium/ still return 200. decodeURIComponent() runs before path resolution, so an encoded traversal attempt is normalized and still caught by the boundary check rather than slipping past it. src/geometry.ts and src/fixture.ts take only numeric lat/lng/height arguments from the test author's own code, not from any external or remote source.
Not applicable — there are no user actions to attribute or deny; this is test tooling run by a developer against their own machine.

The server only serves files under two fixed, non-secret roots (Cesium's bundled Build/Cesium assets and the package's own fixtures/assets/ directory) and the fixed index.html for '/'. It cannot be made to serve anything outside those roots (see Tampering). It binds only to 127.0.0.1 — confirmed in code and by its own comment citing the sibling saturday-playwright-leaflet package's mistake of binding all interfaces, which this implementation deliberately avoids. No secrets, tokens, or PII exist anywhere in this package to disclose.

(egress) The fixture page's CESIUM_BASE_URL is hardcoded to the local '/cesium/' route and the imagery provider loads only the local fixtures/assets/aurelis.jpg — both enforced by a code comment stating 'never a CDN.' No outbound network call exists anywhere in src/ or fixtures/. Nothing in this package can be induced to send data anywhere.

serve.mjs has no request size limits or rate limiting, but it is a local, single-purpose static file server with no write operations, no user uploads, and no internet exposure (127.0.0.1 bind) — a DoS surface here has no attacker to exploit it. waitForSettled()/pollUntilSettled() in fixture.ts take an explicit, caller-supplied timeoutMs with a bounded default (15000ms) rather than an unbounded wait.
No roles, permissions, or privilege levels exist in this package. Not applicable.

findings.title: vitest pinned to an outdated major version, pulling in a vite release with a known High-severity advisory
findings.description: vitest ^2.1.9 resolved to vite <=6.4.3, which carries GHSA-587h-7wmj-h5pm (launch-editor fs.existsSync() bypass on Windows, exploitable only through vite's dev-mode launch-editor middleware). Every other TypeScript package in the monorepo already pins vitest ^4.0.16, so this was version drift introduced by the new package rather than an intentional choice. Low real-world exploitability (dev-only, Windows-specific, requires opening a stack trace in-editor) but it is an unforced, easily-avoided inconsistency, so rated Medium rather than Low.
findings.fixApplied: Bumped the vitest devDependency to ^4.0.16 in packages/saturday-playwright-cesium/package.json and ran pnpm install, which also removed the now-unused vite 5 / esbuild 0.21.5 chain from pnpm-lock.yaml.
findings.verification: `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` no longer lists this package in any finding's Paths column. `pnpm vitest run` still passes all 7 tests in tests/geometry.spec.ts under vitest 4.0.16.

findings.title: Static file server's path-traversal guard confirmed correct by direct test
findings.description: resolveWithinRoot() uses resolve() plus a trailing-separator boundary check, which closes both the raw `../` traversal path and the classic sibling-directory prefix-bypass bug (e.g. root '/foo/bar' matching requests for '/foo/barbaz'). Manually verified against both a raw-encoded and percent-encoded traversal attempt; both returned 404 while legitimate asset requests returned 200. No fix needed — documenting the verification so QA does not need to re-derive it.

securityChecklist.item: No hardcoded secrets, tokens, or credentials anywhere in the package
No authentication, session, or authorization surface exists (verified not applicable)
HTTP server binds to 127.0.0.1 only, not 0.0.0.0 or all interfaces
Static file server rejects path traversal (raw and percent-encoded), verified by direct request
No outbound/egress network calls; imagery and Cesium assets are served locally only, never a CDN
Dependency audit run (pnpm audit --audit-level=high) against the full workspace and scoped to this package's dependency paths
securityChecklist.note: One Medium finding (vitest version drift) found and fixed; re-audited clean for this package afterward.

securityChecklist.item: No new dependency introduces a Critical-severity advisory

notesForQa: No security-driven test additions are required — this package has no auth, input validation, or trust-boundary logic that QA needs to add coverage for beyond what fixture.spec.ts and geometry.spec.ts already exercise.

vitest was bumped from ^2.1.9 to ^4.0.16 to match the rest of the monorepo; re-run the full test command (`pnpm test` in packages/saturday-playwright-cesium) to confirm both the vitest suite and the Playwright fixture suite still pass under the new version — the vitest-only geometry suite was already re-verified in this review.

The fixture server's traversal guard was exercised manually with curl during this review (raw `../` and percent-encoded `%2e%2e%2f`); no automated regression test exists for it. Consider adding one if this server's routing logic is ever extended beyond its current two fixed routes.
